reading.body:
Troy Balderson's AI record is mostly money: 13 of 17 dated events are political committee contributions, and the largest single donor across the period is Amazon at $10,000.

The contributions run from March 2025 to August 2026 and come from the political committees of Amazon, Intel, Google, Meta, Oracle, and Anthropic. Individual amounts are small, between $1,000 and $5,000, and one Meta entry is a $2,000 refund that reverses a $2,000 contribution the day before. The four non-money events are recorded votes, all Yea, on H.R. 7757, H.R. 5764, H.R. 1770, and S. 146. The data does not say what any of those bills do, so no link between a vote and a contribution can be read from this record, and the page states that placement in date order is not a claim of causation.

For AI specifically, the donor list is the tell. Anthropic's committee appears twice, in August 2026, and the rest are the large platform and chip companies whose data centers, models, and hardware sit at the center of the buildout. Money from these committees is a routine feature of congressional politics, not evidence of a deal, and the amounts here are too small to carry one.

What the data does not cover is as important as what it does. It holds no sponsored bills, no committee assignments, no statements, and no votes on the bills' substance, only the fact of a Yea. It also stops at August 2026 for contributions and June 2026 for votes, so it is a partial window rather than a full record.

summary: Every dated AI event this site holds for Troy Balderson: bills sponsored or cosponsored, recorded votes on AI bills, and money from AI company and AI-focused political committees, newest first. 17 events.
